note: Reference densities at 15 °C and the thermal expansion coefficient used to correct them. Confirm against the delivery note or the supplier's data sheet for the fuel actually in the car: a batch varies, and a blend varies more than a batch.
betaSource: Volumetric thermal expansion of light hydrocarbon fuels, 0.00090-0.00100 /°C. Petrol sits near the middle of that range; alcohols are lower. Editable per fuel.

fuels.label: Petrol, unleaded
fuels.source: EN 228 permits 720-775 kg/m3 at 15 °C. 0.745 is the mid-range figure and is a placeholder for a measured one.

fuels.label: E85
fuels.source: Blend of ethanol (0.789) and petrol; the ethanol fraction varies seasonally and with it the density. Measure the batch.

fuels.label: Methanol
fuels.source: Pure methanol at 15 °C. Expands faster than petrol, so the temperature correction matters more, not less.
